_round: Round 12. TWO ORCHESTRATORS EXISTED AT ONCE and this is the record of how it resolved. The weekly limit reset at 21:00 on 2026-09-11; apex-roadmap-resume.timer fired at 21:02 and started an unattended `claude -p` orchestrator (pid 19362) because state/orchestrator.pid was three days stale. An interactive session came up 15 minutes later, found it mid-landing - local roadmap/v2.2 was ahead of origin in BOTH repos - and STOOD DOWN from every write rather than fight it, which is the failure the queue's own comment warns about. The unattended round was the most productive of the program: nine task branches landed, both repos pushed (apex-os 583355e -> 1afd807, apex-shell a90cef6 -> 665a3cc), eleven roadmap items recorded, counts 49/29/47/2 -> 60 done / 24 partial / 41 todo / 2 blocked. It exited cleanly at 21:43:55 saying 'waiting on the six agents now' - so its six agents died with it, and resume.sh still labelled them ALIVE because their .output files were minutes old. The 20-minute mtime heuristic cannot see a dead parent; ps could, and did.

_landed_this_round.apex-os: roadmap/v2.2 1afd807 -> ec91e92, PUSHED. task/editors-desktop-entries, one commit, fast-forward, verified on the landed tip (check-no-conflict-markers PASS, tests/test-apex-editors.sh 14 passed / 1 failed where the single failure IS the defect on this machine - the running image predates the fix and has no Zed entry). This is user-directed work from Andre, not a roadmap unit: 'nvim and zed have to work'. ZED'S HALF IS DIAGNOSED AND FIXED. /usr/bin/zed has been on every APEX machine since stage 5a-zed was written and Zed has never had a launcher entry on any of them - confirmed identically on the L16 and on katana. Containerfile.core installed the entry from zed.app/share/applications/zed.desktop, a name the tarball has NEVER shipped (upstream's is dev.zed.Zed.desktop), and `2>/dev/null || true` swallowed the failure; no icon was installed either. The binary ran fine from a shell, so nothing looked broken from a terminal. The fetch stays non-fatal and that posture is now asserted too, so nobody 'fixes' this by breaking offline builds; everything after a successful unpack is checked - entry present, TryExec names a binary really on PATH, icon resolves in hicolor. Two mutations, both restored byte-identical: M1 the original filename bug 14/1 -> 12/3, M2 the `|| true` swallow alone 14/1 -> 13/2. M2 did NOT bite at first, and that is the finding worth keeping: the assertion grepped one physical line for `install` and another for `|| true`, so it could not fail against the very mutant it existed for. Shell continuations are joined before the structural checks now.

_field_contract: resume.sh does os.path.isdir(worktree) and git rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD, so `worktree` and `branch` must each be ONE value. An agent working two repos records the other in second_worktree/second_branch, which resume.sh ignores. Writing 'a and b' there makes the next report say 'no worktree' for a worktree that is fine.

Not an artifact; a hole in the harness. p0-014's 3c3abd3 suggests it has already started on this class.
